metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights near Southern Ute, CO | San Juan Basin
metaDescription: La Plata County minerals near the Southern Ute reservation sit in the mature San Juan Basin Fruitland coalbed methane play. Get a checkerboard-aware offer.
heroLead: Ownership around Southern Ute is some of the most checkerboarded in Colorado, so a straightforward chain-of-title check matters more here than almost anywhere else in the state.
intro: The San Juan Basin around Ignacio and the Southern Ute Indian Reservation was the epicenter of the Fruitland Formation coalbed methane boom, one of the largest CBM plays in the country through the 1990s and early 2000s. Decades later, the wells are mature, production has declined, and mineral ownership in this area is unusually fragmented between fee interests, tribal allotments, and Southern Ute Indian Tribe-controlled minerals.

sections.heading: Checkerboard ownership and forced pooling
paragraphs: La Plata County land near the reservation is a genuine checkerboard: allotted lands from the original Ute land distributions sit next to fee parcels sold off over the following century, and tribal mineral interests are interspersed with private ones section by section. Because of that fragmentation, forced pooling and communitization agreements have been common tools operators use to bring small, scattered fractional owners into a single producing unit rather than negotiating each parcel separately.

If your interest was pooled at some point, your division order should reflect a specific decimal share of a defined drilling and spacing unit, which is exactly what we use to verify and value your position.

sections.heading: A mature, low-decline gas play
paragraphs: Fruitland CBM wells in this part of the basin are old, most were drilled well over a decade ago, and their production curves have flattened into long, low-volume tails rather than the sharp early decline you'd see in a newer horizontal well. That stability is actually a selling point: a mature CBM royalty is more predictable to value than a brand-new well still working through its decline curve.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest through La Plata County records
paragraphs: Because of the checkerboard history here, we spend extra time on title, pulling your chain through the La Plata County Clerk and Recorder in Durango and checking it against BLM and tribal allotment records where applicable, before we put a number on your interest.

faqs.question: What does checkerboard ownership mean for my sale?
faqs.answer: It means your specific tract's history matters more than a general basin comp. We verify exactly how your parcel was originally conveyed before quoting a price.

faqs.question: Is my interest tribal or fee mineral?
faqs.answer: That depends on the original allotment or conveyance. We check your legal description against county and, where relevant, BLM allotment records to confirm.

faqs.question: Are San Juan Basin CBM wells still producing after this long?
faqs.answer: Many are, at low, stable rates well into their production life, which is actually easier to value with confidence than a newly drilled well.
